claims.text: Integrating graphene nanoplatelets into a high-entropy alloy will reduce its coefficient of friction.
Integrating graphene nanoplatelets into a high-entropy alloy will reduce its wear rate.
The reductions in friction and wear will persist over a broad service-temperature range, including sub-zero and high-temperature extremes.
Sliding will produce a continuous, graphene-rich tribofilm at the contact interface.
Embedded graphene nanoplatelets will segregate to the contact surface during sliding.
The graphene-rich film will reduce direct metal-to-metal interactions.
Reduced direct metal-to-metal interaction and interfacial shear will lower friction.
Reduced direct metal-to-metal interaction and interfacial shear will lower wear.
The graphene-enhanced alloy will exhibit lower friction coefficients than an untreated alloy tested under identical conditions.
The graphene-enhanced alloy will exhibit lower wear rates than an untreated alloy tested under identical conditions.
Inhomogeneous graphene dispersion may reduce the tribological benefits.
Graphene degradation or adverse reaction with the alloy matrix at extreme temperatures may reduce the tribological benefits.
Stresses exceeding the tribofilm's maintenance capability may reduce the tribological benefits.
The magnitude of friction and wear reduction will depend on graphene concentration.
The magnitude of friction and wear reduction will depend on processing quality.
